matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Changing orientation would create an invalid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you move a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick and placing it as a horizontal line, thereby rotating it.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Adding a new stick to form an extra I without removing any stick from another character.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the stick has been placed on its new location.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal after moving a stick away, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and check that the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation.
matchstick.example: Accepting "IV = VII + IV" as correct without noticing that 4 ≠ 11.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals (or be transformed as a whole).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to a V or X.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X, leaving a single diagonal shape.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one character to a different character, altering both; ensure that after the move each character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the source and destination are distinct characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a numeral to an operator but leaving the operator as an undefined shape.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.example: Ending the response with 'Correct version: IX = XIII - IV' instead of the required exact line.

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change from the original can be achieved by moving exactly one stick; no other characters may be altered.
matchstick.example: Changing 'IX' to 'XI' by swapping the two characters, which would require more than one stick move.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave an empty placeholder.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the source character is an I and you intend to take its sole stick.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from an I without deleting the character, leaving a blank space.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transformation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator (+, -, =), ensure the resulting operator is a valid symbol. For example, removing the vertical stick from '+' yields '-', adding a horizontal stick to '-' yields '=', and removing a horizontal stick from '=' yields '-'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the stick being moved originates from or is placed onto an operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' and leaving the remaining horizontal line as an undefined shape, or adding a horizontal stick to '-' without checking that it becomes a valid '='.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual stick manipulation and forgets to check the numeric values of the Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a corrected equation, convert each Roman numeral to its Arabic value and confirm that the arithmetic equality holds.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model adds extra text or deviates from the required final line format.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', using uppercase letters and collapsing whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, explicitly specify both the source character and the destination character, ensuring the stick is placed on the destination.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a numeral that requires a fixed number of sticks, resulting in an incomplete or non‑Roman character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only take sticks from characters that can lose a stick while remaining a valid numeral or operator; respect the fixed‑stick composition of V and X.

matchstick.description: Proposed equation not reachable by a single stick move (multiple sticks changed)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes more than one character or alters character order, which cannot be achieved by moving a single stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compare the original and proposed equations and ensure exactly one stick has been moved, with all other characters unchanged.
